title: Made a 3D chess game with Claude Code where every capture turns into an animated fight
author: vinishkapoor
selftext:
Clashmate is full-rules chess in the browser, but when you take a piece, the two pieces battle it out on the board. Pawns use swords, knights charge on war horses, bishops strike with light, rooks smash the ground, and the queen spins in with her blade. The loser breaks into shards.

**Who made what:**

* **Code, chess rules, computer opponent, weapons and board:** made with Claude Code
* **Characters and motions:** Mixamo
* **War horse:** Quaternius (CC0)
* **Textures and sky:** Poly Haven (CC0)
* **Sounds and music:** Freesound (CC0)

**What worked:** keeping the chess engine and the fight animations completely separate. The rules came first (castling, en passant, promotion, threefold repetition, the fifty-move rule) and were tested with no animation at all. The fights were added on top, so they can be skipped or switched to fast captures without touching the game logic.

There are five computer levels, from Squire to Grandmaster, plus two players on one screen.

[https://vinish.dev/clashmate-animated-chess-browser-based-game](https://vinish.dev/clashmate-animated-chess-browser-based-game)

replies.author: sillygoofygooose
replies.body: Yep! Back to the 80's! The thing about this is - unless you make a chess-*like* where clash outcomes can vary in some way the animation quickly becomes annoying as it has nothing to do with the actual gameplay.

comments.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
comments.body: I think ive seen several chess games that do this, my gripe isnt that its AI but that it just isnt a interesting concept, think of it like this, why would i play this when games that do exactly this already exist?
